content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves the pressed Luke 2:48-49 witness by an immediate clause-to-clause qualification, which is the verse-by-verse move the rule governs when a pressed link must instead be weighed chain against chain by footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"`never verse by verse` — one reading bars immediate qualification of one clause by the next as a way to resolve a pressed link; the other permits it as contextual reading. I weighed these and treat the judge's immediate qualification as the barred verse-by-verse resolution.","why":"The judge answers the Luke 2:48-49 collision by saying Mary's phrase is immediately qualified by the next clause, rather than by weighing chain against chain by footing as K-C requires."}
